svg.title: Use a recessive tester to compare two possible genotypes
svg.desc: Two explicit models compare an unknown AA or Aa parent crossed with an aa tester. AA produces only A gametes and all Aa offspring. Aa produces A or a gametes with equal probability and therefore half Aa and half aa offspring. An aa offspring requires a from the unknown parent and identifies Aa under the simple fully specified model. Four dominant outcomes can still occur under Aa×aa with probability(1/2)^4=1/16 for independent trials, so an all-dominant small sample does not prove AA. The cross depends on its expression and scoring assumptions, not a universal human-trait rule.

g.text: Use a recessive tester to compare two possible genotypes
The same dominant phenotype can hide different allele combinations.
Unknown dominant-phenotype parent: AA or Aa
Tester: aa, so every tester gamete carries a.
A + a → Aa (½); a + a → aa (½)
An aa offspring shows that the unknown parent supplied a, under this model.
All dominant offspring in a small sample do not prove that the unknown parent was AA.
For Aa × aa, four dominant outcomes in four independent trials have probability (½)⁴ = 1/16.
Specify the locus, trait scoring and parental genotypes before interpreting any ratio.
